according to; based on (casual conditional/source marker)
to board; to get on (a vehicle)

grammar_patterns.explanation: 「～ていたことになる」 — 「ことになる」 expresses a logical conclusion derived from available facts, a hallmark of L's deductive speech pattern. Very characteristic of detective register.

appearing to be; seemingly (attributive form of らしい, more literary)
to hold in one's hand; to have in hand

vocabulary.meaning: just before death; immediately prior to death

belongings left behind; found personal effects (police term)
it amounts to; it logically follows

grammar_patterns.explanation: 「よく～ましたね」 is a set compliment pattern ('well done noticing'). 「～ということになる」 again is L's deductive conclusion marker. 「それとこのペンバーの最後のビデオ」 is an additive transition to a new point.

to appear to be; looks like

translation: S-surely not... / I also think it's surely not the case.

vocabulary.meaning: surely not; no way; that can't be (expression of disbelief)

grammar: 「まさか」 stands alone as an exclamation of disbelief. 「まさかとは思います」 — L concedes the unlikelihood: 'I also think it's a stretch.' The stutter 「ま、まさか」 shows the task force member's shock.

grammar_patterns.explanation: 「まさか」 stands alone as an exclamation of disbelief. 「まさかとは思います」 — L concedes the unlikelihood: 'I also think it's a stretch.' The stutter 「ま、まさか」 shows the task force member's shock.

text: 遠隔で死を操れるキラがわざわざ現場にいるはずがない

vocabulary.meaning: going out of one's way; taking the trouble to
the scene (of a crime); on site
there is no way that; cannot possibly be

to take action; to make a move

the moment; just as; as soon as

text: おはようございます
translation: Good morning.

vocabulary.meaning: good morning (polite form; used in professional settings throughout the day in media/entertainment contexts)

grammar: Standard polite morning greeting. In Japanese broadcasting/media workplaces, おはようございます can be used any time of day as a professional greeting. Here, used in its literal sense.
